**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive callback redirect URI instead of requiring query param**

The callback handler currently requires `redirectUri` from `resolveCallbackInput` or `?redirectUri=...`, but standard OAuth callbacks only send `code` and `state`. With the default route config (as shown in the package quick start), this path throws before `flowService.handleCallback` runs, so normal provider callbacks fail (and become 500s because a plain `Error` is thrown). This breaks out-of-the-box callback handling unless every consumer adds custom callback input resolution.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate provider matches token record before disconnect delete**

`disconnect()` looks up the token only by `connectionId` and then always deletes it, but never verifies that `tokenRecord.record.providerId` matches `input.providerId`. If a stale or incorrect provider is passed (for example via `:provider` path mismatch), the service can delete a different provider’s token and skip/revoke against the wrong upstream provider. This should fail fast on provider mismatch before local deletion.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-throw adapter failures when consuming OAuth state**

The `consume()` implementation swallows every `adapter.update()` error and returns `null`, which makes infrastructure or query failures look like “state not found/expired.” Upstream this is mapped to user-facing OAuth state errors instead of surfacing a storage failure, so real DB outages become misleading 4xx auth failures and lose retry/debug signals. Only “not found” should be converted to `null`; unexpected adapter errors should be re-thrown.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

P1: `rotateKey` updates only `key_ref` without re-encrypting `encrypted_payload`. After this call, the stored payload is still encrypted with the old key but `key_ref` points to the new key, making the token un-decryptable on the next `get()`. `EncryptedTokenVault` never calls this method (it uses `put`), so when called directly on `DbAdapterTokenVault` it silently corrupts data. Consider either implementing the full decrypt-reencrypt-store cycle or documenting/restricting this method as internal-only.

+import type {
+  OAuthConsentRecord,
+  OAuthConsentStore,

+  validateOAuthStateRecord,
+  validateOAuthStoredSubject
+} from "../state-store.js";
+
+export interface SqlResult {
+  rowsAffected?: number;
+}
+
+export interface SqlClient {
+  query<TRow = unknown>(statement: string, params?: readonly unknown[]): Promise<TRow[]>;
+  execute(statement: string, params?: readonly unknown[]): Promise<SqlResult>;
+}
+
+interface OAuthStateRow {
+  state_id: string;

+  subject_kind: string;

+  retryable: boolean;
+  occurred_at: string;

+}

+const STATE_COLUMNS = `
+  state_id,

+  redirect_uri,
+  requested_scopes,

+const TOKEN_COLUMNS = `

+  encrypted_payload,

+const CONSENT_COLUMNS = `

+  subject_key,
+  subject_payload,
+  scope_set,
+  granted_at,

+const REVOCATION_FAILURE_COLUMNS = `
+  failure_id,
+  provider_id,
+  subject_kind,
+  subject_key,
+  subject_payload,
+  token_id,
+  token_type_hint,
+  error_code,
+  error_message,
+  retryable,
+  occurred_at,
+  metadata
+`;
+
+export class SqlOAuthStateStore implements OAuthStateStore {
+  private readonly client: SqlClient;
+  private readonly tableName: string;
+
+  constructor(client: SqlClient, tableName = "oauth_states") {
+    this.client = client;
+    this.tableName = tableName;
+  }
+
+  async put(record: OAuthStateRecord): Promise<void> {
+    validateOAuthStateRecord(record);
+    const normalized = applySubjectToStateRecord(record);
+    await this.client.execute(
+      `
+      INSERT INTO ${this.tableName} (
+        state_id,
+        provider_id,
+        subject_kind,
+        subject_key,
+        subject_payload,
+        redirect_uri,
+        requested_scopes,
+        code_verifier,
+        nonce,
+        created_at,
+        expires_at,
+        consumed_at
+      ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+      ON CONFLICT(state_id) DO UPDATE SET
+        provider_id = excluded.provider_id,
+        subject_kind = excluded.subject_kind,
+        subject_key = excluded.subject_key,
+        subject_payload = excluded.subject_payload,
+        redirect_uri = excluded.redirect_uri,
+        requested_scopes = excluded.requested_scopes,
+        code_verifier = excluded.code_verifier,
+        nonce = excluded.nonce,
+        created_at = excluded.created_at,
+        expires_at = excluded.expires_at,
+        consumed_at = excluded.consumed_at
+      `,
+      [
+        normalized.stateId,
+        normalized.providerId,
+        normalized.subject!.kind,
+        getOAuthSubjectKey(normalized.subject!),
+        JSON.stringify(normalized.subject),
+        normalized.redirectUri,
+        JSON.stringify(normalized.requestedScopes),
+        normalized.codeVerifier ?? null,
+        normalized.nonce ?? null,
+        normalized.createdAt,
+        normalized.expiresAt,
+        normalized.consumedAt ?? null
+      ]
+    );
+  }
+
+  async get(stateId: string): Promise<OAuthStateRecord | null> {
+    const rows = await this.client.query<OAuthStateRow>(
+      `SELECT ${STATE_COLUMNS} FROM ${this.tableName} WHERE state_id = ? LIMIT 1`,
+      [stateId]
+    );
+
+    return rows[0] ? mapStateRow(rows[0]) : null;
+  }
+
+  async consume(stateId: string, consumedAt: string): Promise<OAuthStateRecord | null> {
+    const rows = await this.client.query<OAuthStateRow>(
+      `
+      UPDATE ${this.tableName}
+      SET consumed_at = ?
+      WHERE state_id = ?
+        AND consumed_at IS NULL
+        AND expires_at > ?
+      RETURNING ${STATE_COLUMNS}
+      `,
+      [consumedAt, stateId, consumedAt]
+    );
+
+    return rows[0] ? mapStateRow(rows[0]) : null;
+  }
+
+  async deleteExpired(before: string): Promise<number> {
+    const result = await this.client.execute(`DELETE FROM ${this.tableName} WHERE expires_at < ?`, [before]);
+    return result.rowsAffected ?? 0;
+  }
+}
+
+export class SqlTokenVault implements TokenVault {
+  private readonly client: SqlClient;
+  private readonly tableName: string;
+
+  constructor(client: SqlClient, tableName = "oauth_tokens") {
+    this.client = client;
+    this.tableName = tableName;
+  }
+
+  async put(record: TokenRecord): Promise<void> {
+    await this.client.execute(
+      `
+      INSERT INTO ${this.tableName} (
+        token_id,
+        tenant_id,
+        user_id,
+        provider_id,
+        connection_id,
+        encrypted_payload,
+        key_ref,
+        created_at,
+        updated_at,
+        expires_at
+      ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+      ON CONFLICT(token_id) DO UPDATE SET
+        tenant_id = excluded.tenant_id,
+        user_id = excluded.user_id,
+        provider_id = excluded.provider_id,
+        connection_id = excluded.connection_id,
+        encrypted_payload = excluded.encrypted_payload,
+        key_ref = excluded.key_ref,
+        created_at = excluded.created_at,
+        updated_at = excluded.updated_at,
+        expires_at = excluded.expires_at
+      `,
+      [
+        record.tokenId,
+        record.tenantId,
+        record.userId,
+        record.providerId,
+        record.connectionId,
+        record.encryptedPayload,
+        record.keyRef,
+        record.createdAt,
+        record.updatedAt,
+        record.expiresAt ?? null
+      ]
+    );
+  }
+
+  async get(tokenId: string): Promise<TokenRecord | null> {
+    const rows = await this.client.query<TokenRow>(
+      `SELECT ${TOKEN_COLUMNS} FROM ${this.tableName} WHERE token_id = ? LIMIT 1`,
+      [tokenId]
+    );
+
+    return rows[0] ? mapTokenRow(rows[0]) : null;
+  }
+
+  async getByConnection(connectionId: string): Promise<TokenRecord | null> {
+    const rows = await this.client.query<TokenRow>(
+      `SELECT ${TOKEN_COLUMNS} FROM ${this.tableName} WHERE connection_id = ? LIMIT 1`,
+      [connectionId]
+    );
+
+    return rows[0] ? mapTokenRow(rows[0]) : null;
+  }
+
+  async rotateKey(tokenId: string, newKeyRef: string): Promise<void> {
+    await this.client.execute(
+      `UPDATE ${this.tableName} SET key_ref = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE token_id = ?`,
+      [newKeyRef, new Date().toISOString(), tokenId]
+    );
+  }
+
+  async deleteByConnection(connectionId: string): Promise<void> {
+    await this.client.execute(`DELETE FROM ${this.tableName} WHERE connection_id = ?`, [connectionId]);
+  }
+}
+
+export class SqlOAuthConsentStore implements OAuthConsentStore {
+  private readonly client: SqlClient;

+    this.client = client;
+    this.tableName = tableName;
+  }
+
+  async put(record: OAuthConsentRecord): Promise<void> {
+    validateOAuthConsentRecord(record);
+    await this.client.execute(
+      `
+      INSERT INTO ${this.tableName} (
+        consent_id,
+        provider_id,
+        subject_kind,
+        subject_key,
+        subject_payload,
+        scope_set,
+        granted_at,
+        updated_at,
+        metadata
+      ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)

**Empty allowlist silently permits all redirect URIs** When `allowlistedRedirectUris` is an empty array the function returns immediately, accepting any redirect URI the caller supplies. A provider whose runtime config omits or accidentally clears `allowlistedRedirectUris` will pass validation for every URI — including attacker-controlled ones — enabling an open-redirect and authorization-code interception attack. The safer default is to treat an empty allowlist as _deny-all_, or require callers to explicitly pass a wildcard sentinel to opt into unrestricted mode: ```suggestion export function assertRedirectUriAllowed(redirectUri: string, allowlistedRedirectUris: ReadonlyArray): void { if (!allowlistedRedirectUris.includes(redirectUri)) { throw new OAuthCoreError("OAUTH_REDIRECT_DISALLOWED", "redirect URI not allowed"); } ```
